CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, 2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended (PCMLTA) and associated FINTRAC Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31 (money laundering offence); Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), as amended, including the unlimited liability corporation provisions and Part 1, Division 2.1 (Individuals with Significant Control register, in force 1 April 2023); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4 (ISC register for federally-incorporated entities); United Nations Act, SC 1999, c 5; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled certified copy of passport or national identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin; apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority under the Hague Apostille Convention (e.g., U.S. Department of State for U.S. documents; Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office for U.K. documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded 12 May 2023; Convention in force for Canada since 14 January 2024); documents from non-Hague states require full Consular Legalization via the Consular Section of the Government of Canada mission or the issuing state's foreign ministry double-authentication chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence for each foreign corporate shareholder in the piercing chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies in each shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations for U.S. holding companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and unanimous shareholder resolution authorizing the Alberta ULC incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary / authorized officer of the parent entity, notarized by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter, source-of-funds declaration, and AML/KYC pack for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution or licensed service provider in the UBO's residence jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or banker's certification accepted subject to FINTRAC risk assessment; Consular Legalization only if required by the receiving counterparty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory of the Alberta ULC against: (i) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), and the United Nations Act; (iv) FINTRAC published advisories on money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions evasion; (v) the Criminal Code and PCMLTA definitions of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), requiring enhanced due diligence for any PEP class UBO or board member; (vi) OSFI and FINTRAC Guidance (including FINTRAC Guidance on politically exposed persons); and (vii) Alberta Court of King's Bench and provincial securities commission enforcement records. Standard Due Diligence applies for the Low_Risk_Standard stevedoring tier, with a mandatory 5-year record retention period and designation of an AML compliance officer at the entity level.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES - Corporate Registry System) operated by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) real-time reports obtained through authorized NUANS service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English and/or French using the Latin alphabet (Roman script) and Arabic numerals; names in other scripts must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters for NUANS processing. The name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element (optional), and a legal element. For an Alberta ULC the legal element must be 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or the abbreviation 'ULC' or 'SRI'. The word 'The' may be used at the front of the name. Commas, periods, and apostrophes are disregarded for distinctiveness. A name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate name, reserved name, trademark, or registered business name in Alberta.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banker, trust, loan, credit, insurance, assurance, co-operative, college, university, institute, council, association, medical, condominium, homestead, municipal, police, Royal, Crown, government, or any word implying connection with the Crown, the Government of Alberta, a municipal authority, or a professional regulatory body - all requiring prior ministerial, superintendent, or regulatory body consent
Obscene, grossly offensive, misleading, or publicly objectionable expressions per the Registrar's discretion under ABCA corporate name policy
Names implying a different legal structure (e.g., partnership, firm, société en nom collectif) prohibited for a ULC
Statutorily restricted terms such as 'condominium', 'homeowners' association', 'quarterly', and 'co-op' absent specific statutory authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the incorporator receives a Registrar's refusal statement. The applicant may file a written request for administrative re-consideration with Service Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the refusal, submitting a fresh NUANS report (valid 90 days), legal arguments distinguishing prior marks, and any necessary third-party consent letters. The applicant may also renew the name reservation for an additional 90-day period by paying the applicable renewal fee and obtaining a new NUANS report. If the administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may: (i) select a new name and re-file, preserving the original incorporation filing fee on refiling; or (ii) appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by way of originating application under the ABCA and the Alberta Rules of Court, seeking an order that the Registrar accept the name. An appeal should be commenced within 30 days of the reconsideration refusal date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only if the virtual office provides a physical street address in Alberta (not a P.O. Box) where legal process and notices can be served in person during business hours; pure mailbox addresses are non-compliant with ABCA registered office requirements. For the bulk port stevedoring terminal industry, the registered office may legitimately be a licensed corporate service-provider address in Alberta, provided the actual terminal operations procure a berth/terminal lease with the applicable Port Authority and maintain tangible operational assets, inventory, and staff in Canada. A virtual office alone will not satisfy the commercial substance test applied by the Canada Revenue Agency for tax treaty access, nor the diligence standards of port authorities, marine insurers, and lending counterparties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk of approximately 15% annual probability per registered office, based on Alberta Corporate Registry desk audits, FINTRAC compliance examination protocols (primarily documentary but may include on-site visits of record-keepers), and routine Port Authority lease compliance inspections at the stevedoring terminal. Unannounced physical on-site inspection of the registered office by the Alberta Corporate Registry is rare but legally permitted under the Registrar's information-gathering powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 8, 12-13, 15.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporation provisions) and 101; supplemental Ministerial and Corporate Registry procedures
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta (online portal: Alberta Corporate Access)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation for an Unlimited Liability Corporation, filed together with the prescribed Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for nominal, cash, or non-cash consideration as resolved by the board. The defining statutory feature is the shareholders' unlimited liability for the ULC's debts, which enables U.S. federal tax classification as a disregarded entity or partnership under U.S. Treasury Regulation section 301.7701-3.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accept the subscribers' offers to subscribe for 100 common shares without par value for aggregate consideration of CAD 100, issue the shares fully paid, and record all subscriptions and the paid-up capital in the share register. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at [registered address] in Calgary, Alberta, and that the prescribed Notice of Registered Office be filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry. RESOLVED, that [Director A] and [Director B] be appointed as directors and that [President], [Secretary], and [Chief Financial Officer] be appointed as officers with powers and duties set out in Bylaw No. 1. RESOLVED, that the officers execute all banking resolutions, engage the registered agent, and file all corporate and regulatory declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Registry, Service Alberta) via the Alberta Corporate Access portal or a licensed service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation request proposing up to three names ending with the ULC designator 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'; the registry performs a NUANS search against existing corporate names and registered trademarks; once approved, the name is reserved for 90 days and must be cited in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names with ULC designator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as confusingly similar, file a new reservation using a distinct distinctive first or second word, or rely on an already reserved alternative name before the reservation expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - online filing through Alberta Corporate Access
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file Form 1 Articles of Incorporation for an unlimited liability corporation, stating the ULC election, share conditions, restrictions on business activities limited to stevedoring, port terminal operations, and related cargo logistics, the number of directors (minimum one), and the registered office address; attach the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors; pay the statutory fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number.
required_dossiers: Consents of directors to act in office
Registered office address consent from landlord or agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency query or correction notice, respond within 20 days via the ACA portal with amended articles or explanatory materials; if the certificate is refused, refile after rectifying the identified share condition or business restriction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of the Corporation acting by written resolution under section 114 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or circulate a written resolution) to adopt Bylaw No. 1, approve the issuance and allotment of shares, record paid-up capital, appoint officers, fix the fiscal year end, adopt the corporate seal, order the corporate minute book, and open the registers of shareholders, directors, and officers; the EPC must witness the signing of the first board resolution and file the resolution and meeting minutes into the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is disqualified under section 105 (age, bankruptcy, or capacity), remove the director by shareholder ordinary resolution, appoint a qualified replacement, and file an updated Notice of Directors with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fiscal, Payroll, and Workers Compensation Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration / WCB Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA through the Business Registration Online portal to obtain the federal Business Number, and open the GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll deduction accounts; thereafter register for the Alberta corporate tax account and the WCB Alberta industry classification account for marine cargo handling and stevedoring, and file the appropriate remittance and reporting schedules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the registration, respond through the BRO portal with supporting corporate documents within 30 days; if the WCB classification is disputed, appeal the assessment within 30 days with operational descriptions and payroll records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal, Port, and Landside Operational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable municipal business licensing authority; the relevant port authority (marine or inland port facility); Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; Alberta OHS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence for cargo handling and stevedoring operations, execute the terminal concession or lease at the operating marine or inland port site, and obtain the appropriate environmental registration, fire safety, structural, and OHS clearances for the Alberta head office, storage yards, and any landside dry-port facilities; all licences must name the Alberta ULC as licensee.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaw No. 1
Fire Code and OHS clearance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the port authority conditions the concession, negotiate a compliance and abatement schedule; if the environmental registration is refused, upgrade to a full environmental impact assessment or a sectoral approval as demanded by the regulator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada - Marine Safety and Security (federal); the applicable port authority for the terminal site; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for Alberta provincial environmental matters regarding landside facilities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Terminal Operating Licence and Port Stevedoring Concession under Part 2 of the Canada Marine Act, SC 1998, c 10, port authority bylaws and lease agreements; supplementary municipal cargo handling business licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-tier environmental approval (Category B facility) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 for landside bulk cargo storage; a federal impact assessment is assessed under the Impact Assessment Act, SC 2019, c 28 if the operational marine berth expansion exceeds screening thresholds or affects fish habitat under the Fisheries Act; the physical marine berth is expected to be sited in a coastal province, which will require that province's environmental review in addition to this Alberta head-office registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero untreated discharge of process wastewater; any discharge to municipal sewer must meet the applicable sewer use bylaw limits; ballast water management at any marine berth must satisfy IMO D-2 standards; fugitive dust and particulate emission controls required for dry bulk cargo handling; National Pollutant Release Inventory reporting triggered above 10 tonnes per year; storage and handling of dangerous goods must comply with the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations and WHMIS labelling standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code certification for terminal buildings, warehouses, and administrative premises; structural engineering certificate for cargo handling cranes, gantries, berth aprons, and haul roads; Occupational Health and Safety clearance from Alberta OHS covering stevedoring and cargo handling processes; Marine Transportation Security Regulations clearance (MARSEC) for credentialed terminal workers; approved first aid, fire response, and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal tax authority; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance administers provincial corporate tax. Official portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian ULCs obtain Business Number (BN) from CRA immediately upon incorporation or registration with Alberta corporate registry. Foreign entities register online via CRA My Business Account or by mail to secure GST/HST number and BN if carrying on business in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No standard check-the-box election available; Canadian corporations including ULCs are subject to entity-level taxation under Income Tax Act. Limited election possible to treat qualifying entity as partnership for tax purposes under section 216 if all conditions satisfied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Registrants issue tax invoices on request and file GST/HST returns electronically through CRA My Business Account. API integration not required for standard compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for 0% GST rate. Offshore services zero-rated if performed entirely outside Canada with no Canadian consideration. Strict substantiation required including proof of export and remittance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may result in reassessment; penalties range from 10% to 200% of tax due for gross negligence or fraudulent claims, plus interest and retrospective clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime under the Bank of Canada Act. Both capital and current accounts are unrestricted; profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior approval, subject only to tax filing and beneficial ownership reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required. Exporters may retain foreign exchange receipts; voluntary conversion through authorized dealers is available. All transactions must be reported to the Canada Revenue Agency and comply with FINTRAC AML obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed in Canada. Platforms such as Wise provide cross-border rails but require Canadian entities to route through licensed banks. Legal constraints include FINTRAC registration and prohibition on direct EMI banking services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signers must appear in person for KYC interviews at bank branches; remote opening is not permitted for non-resident directors or ULC entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media screening hit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds evidence, beneficial ownership certificate, and legal opinion confirming non-sanctioned status
Enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth documentation and board-level approval

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires beneficial ownership declaration, corporate charter, and tax identification confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for payments and Commercial Letters of Credit for secured disbursements. All outflows must comply with export controls and transfer-pricing documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Certificate of Compliance) under ABCA s.263
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 months after incorporation; thereafter within 15 months after the date on which the last annual return was required to be filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 250 late-filing penalty per overdue return; continued non-filing may trigger administrative dissolution by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta corporate income tax, filed jointly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., December 31 year-end: due June 30 of the following calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (17% cap); repeat failures double to 10% plus 2% per month; interest compounded daily at the prescribed CRA rate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and Reconciliation (annual filer election)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year for annual GST/HST filers; otherwise per assigned monthly/quarterly frequency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 or 1% of net tax owing, charged per complete month late up to 12 months, plus interest compounded daily on unremitted amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Port Terminal Operator / Stevedoring Licence Annual Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Port Authority (e.g., Port of Edmonton inland port authority) and Transport Canada Marine Safety
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of the terminal operating agreement or stevedoring licence, as stipulated in the authorizing instrument
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expiry or revocation of berthing/stevedoring authorization; immediate operational suspension until reinstatement; port tariff arrears subject to access denial

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a private Alberta ULC where all shareholders pass a unanimous resolution dispensing with an auditor (ABCA s.162); audit may be contractually required by lenders, Port Authority concession terms, or bondholders
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private enterprises; IFRS if the ULC has public debt/securities or the port authority agreement mandates IFRS reporting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ULCs must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and update it within 15 days of any share transfer or control change; the Alberta Annual Return functions as the annual confirmation by requiring current shareholder, director, officer, and ISC information to be declared to the Corporate Registry
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book (minutes of directors and shareholders meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 260 – 675 (typical annual registered office and registered agent services in Alberta)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000 – 45,000 (where audit is required by lenders or concession agreements; CAD 0 if the unanimous waiver under ABCA s.162 is in effect)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta provincial general corporate rate = 23% combined headline rate (non-CCPC; Alberta tax administered by the CRA)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general Alberta provincial tax holiday. Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) can claim the Small Business Deduction: 9% federal rate on active business income up to $500,000 and 2% Alberta small business rate on the same $500,000 limit (Alberta small business limit aligned at $500,000). Additional incentives include Investment Tax Credits (ITCs) for SR&ED under ITA s.127, Atlantic Investment Tax Credit where applicable, accelerated CCA classes, and the federal/AB clean economy and manufacturing ITCs. A foreign-owned ULC will normally not qualify as a CCPC and thus receives the flat 23% combined rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through CRA's 'My Business Account' / 'Represent a Client' portal using EFILE or authorized E-filer; Alberta corporate income tax is integrated into the T2 and administered by the CRA under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement (no separate Alberta filing). Mandatory e-filing applies to corporations with gross revenue over CAD 1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (taxation year is the fiscal year); estimated tax instalments are due monthly/quarterly under ITA s.156 (monthly or quarterly instalments for non-CCPCs and CCPCs depending on prior-year tax payable).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 filing due no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end (ITA s.150(1)); balance of Part I tax due within 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and within 3 months for CCPCs entitled to the Small Business Deduction (ITA s.157(1)). Example: a December 31 year-end requires filing by June 30 and final payment by February 28 (non-CCPC).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 jacket, Page 1, Box 100 and Box 110
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 100: full legal name of the corporation; Box 110: nine-digit Business Number / corporate account (e.g., 123456789RC0001).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the ULC's registered legal name in Canada; if registered under Alberta's Business Corporations Act as an unlimited liability corporation, use the exact certificate name. The Business Number must include the 'RC' program identifier for corporate income tax. Non-resident directors' jurisdiction codes, if any, are entered in Schedule 4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of the taxation year-end in YYYY-MM-DD format; the return covers the complete 12-month period unless a stub-period return is required for incorporation or change of year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ULC treated as a check-the-box disregarded entity by its US parent, still file a full 12-month Canadian T2 using the Canadian fiscal period; Canadian entity-level residency remains based on place of incorporation and central management and control in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 jacket, Box 300 (gross revenue) and Schedule 125 (Income Statement)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from stevedoring services, marine cargo handling, dockage demurrage and ancillary terminal charges; Schedule 125 reconciles the income statement to the financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue in Canadian dollars. For foreign-currency receivables, use the CRA's prescribed annual exchange rates. Non-resident-owned ULCs must ensure arm's-length fees for port services are not artificially deflated to shift profit out of Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 jacket, Box 350 (net income before taxes) / Schedule 1 (Tax Calculation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed after deducting all eligible operating expenses (wages, lease/throughput agreements, maintenance, depreciation under CCA rules, interest) and after adding/deducting the consolidation adjustments on Schedule 1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot allocate losses to the ULC on the Canadian return. The ULC computes Canadian taxable income on a stand-alone basis. Thin capitalization rules under ITA s.78(4)-(7) and the new Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL) restrict interest deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 jacket, Box 360 (federal income tax) and Schedule 1, Part II
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base federal Part I tax at 15% on taxable income, reduced by any applicable Small Business Deduction (9% on up to $500,000 for CCPCs), SR&ED ITCs and other refundable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A ULC with foreign ownership is presumed not to be a CCPC; therefore the Small Business Deduction is generally unavailable. Claim only federal ITCs for qualifying port-related capital investments if statutory eligibility tests are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 jacket, Box 385 (Alberta provincial income tax) and Schedule 5, Alberta Part
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate income tax computed at 8% on Alberta taxable income. Alberta does not maintain a separate return; Schedule 5 calculated in the T2 is the exclusive filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Alabama (sic) Alberta imposes no separate capital tax and applies a flat 8% rate for general corporations. Foreign shareholders cannot claim a provincial tax exemption; Canadian-source business income remains subject to Alberta tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 jacket, Box 400 (total tax payable), Box 476 (instalments paid), Box 480 (balance due)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 400 is the sum of federal and provincial tax payable; Box 476 records instalments already paid; Box 480 is the remittance balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ULCs must use the CRA's Race/EFT protocols? Actually: remit via electronic funds transfer using pre-authorized debit or CRA Web payments; if no Canadian-payroll branch, set up a corporate tax account. Instalments are calculated on the prior-year's tax liability under s.156.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under ITA s.162(1): 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month of delay (maximum 12 months); repeated failure: 10% on the first offence? Actually, the penalty is 5% plus 1% per month up to 12 months (max 17%). Late payment interest charged at the CRA prescribed daily compound rate (currently ~9% for 2024-25). Failure to remit Part XIII withholding tax triggers a 10% penalty on withheld amounts plus interest; gross negligence penalty under s.163(2) is 50% of any tax understated; criminal prosecution under s.239 can reach 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment.
